title: Nova - Postmortem / Incident Follow-up
summary: Follow-up on the Dec 9th production incident that caused elevated latency and partial failures for Nova's embedding and chat routes. Reviewed root cause (KV cache memory leak + fallback race), mitigations applied (hotfix, config changes, emergency rollback), and next reliability improvements. Agreed on runbook updates, longer-term code fix timeline, and a joint benchmark to validate the patch in a staging cluster.
action_items: Diego Morales: Produce deterministic repro steps and a minimal test harness by 2026-12-20
Redwood SE team: Share hotfix patch diff and deployment notes by 2026-12-17
Priya Patel: Schedule joint staging benchmark session for week of 2026-12-22
Maya Chen: Provide three representative production prompt sets by 2026-12-18
Samira Khan: Share incident timeline and customer-facing postmortem draft by 2026-12-19
next_steps: Redwood to push hotfix to staging and run benchmarks with Nova datasets
Customer to validate patch on staging and confirm SLO recovery
Schedule runbook review and update on-call escalation flow
Exchange SOC2/ISO audit logs snippet and KMS call traces as follow-up docs
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-15 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~46m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Redwood CSM), Liam O'Connor (Nova SRE), Maya Chen (Nova MLOps), Carlos Ruiz (Nova Eng Manager)

[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is the postmortem follow-up from the outage on Dec 9th. We wanted to walk through what we found, what we patched, and agree next steps. Diego, want to kick off with the timeline?

[00:18] Diego: Yep. Quick TL;DR - root cause is a memory leak in the KV cache eviction path that only surfaced under Nova's median sequence lengths and heavy prefix caching. That leaked until the process hit OOM and then we saw the fallback logic hit a race that dropped some requests. We also had a secondary issue where the KMS token refresh hit a transient error which amplified failures for request signing for a short window.

[00:42] Maya: Sorry, can you repeat the KMS bit? I thought KMS was only advisory.

[00:46] Diego: Sure — the K M S refresh token call had a transient 503 from the provider. Most requests retried fine, but combined with the degraded CPU when the process was swapping it pushed some signing requests over the retry budget. So some requests failed heading into the model runtime.

[01:05] Liam: From our end we saw elevated tail latency starting around 02:12 UTC and full error spike at 02:28. Our alerts triggered and we opened the incident. We appreciate the quick rollback you executed. Can you describe exactly what you rolled back?

[01:23] Samira: We rolled back the runtime build with the new eviction heuristics to the previous stable build and also disabled aggressive prefix caching for Nova's tenant for the short term. That brought latency back down in ~8 minutes. Diego, you applied a hotfix after?

[01:37] Diego: Right, hotfix was a patch to the KV cache allocator — it bounds the growth and adds a defensive guard to avoid double-free in the eviction path. We also added additional telemetry and an early OOM sentinel to trigger a graceful restart before the runtime becomes unresponsive. Patch was rolled to canary and then to prod cutover.

[01:58] Carlos: Quick question — was this specific to Nova's traffic profile? We saw you mention median sequence length and heavy prefix caching. Would other customers be affected?

[02:08] Diego: It's a combination of memory pattern and workload. We saw similar signals in internal tests but they didn't reach the OOM threshold. Nova's mix—longer prompts plus dense caching—pushed it over. We believe other tenants are at lower risk but we'll scan for similar signal across top 30 tenants.

[02:27] Maya: From compliance perspective, did the KMS transient cause any key use errors? We need audit traces for the period for our security team.

[02:35] Priya: Yes, we'll share the KMS call logs and audit traces. Note there was no key compromise; just transient failures and retries. We'll redact sensitive token material and provide the traces.

[02:49] Liam: Thanks. Also, on the incident timeline in the customer-facing postmortem, we want clear phrasing around cause vs contributing factors. We also want to understand the SLA impact per route — embeddings vs chat — to reconcile with our internal SLOs.

[03:06] Samira: Understood, we'll include per-route metrics. For Nova we saw embeddings had higher error rate briefly because of the way we route those requests through the cache layer. Chat experienced higher latency but fewer permanent failures.

[03:20] Carlos: Can you walk through the fallback behavior? We noticed a lot of 500s rather than graceful degraded results.

[03:28] Diego: Yeah that's part of the postmortem. There was a race between fallback to a lightweight model variant and the cache eviction path which left some requests half-processed. Hotfix adds locks and better failure semantics so fallback is deterministic. We'll also add metrics to ensure fallback success rate is tracked.

[03:51] Maya: We need to know what changes on our side, if any. Should we change client retry settings? Increase timeouts?

[03:57] Diego: Short-term we recommend increasing client-side retries to 3 with exponential backoff and bumping connect/read timeouts by 20% for the next two weeks while we validate the patch. We'll send suggested config snippets.

[04:16] Priya: Action item — we'll send the recommended client retry/timeouts and a sample config to your SRE team.

[04:24] Liam: Good. Also, what's the ETA for the root-cause code fix vs the hotfix? We need timeline for permanent remediation.

[04:31] Diego: Hotfix is deployed and mitigates the immediate issue; the full refactor to the eviction algorithm and additional unit tests is targeted for a 3-week window — estimating code complete by 2027-01-05 and rollout by 2027-01-12, barring regressions.

[04:49] Carlos: Who owns that in Redwood? Who should we contact during the rollout?

[04:53] Samira: Diego will own the change, and Priya will coordinate release communications. Samira as AE will coordinate priority and escalation.

[05:05] Maya: On the security front, will this patch affect our compliance posture? We want to ensure no new audit gaps.

[05:12] Diego: No changes to key management or encryption behavior. The patch is purely memory-management and telemetry. We'll add an audit entry and share the change log with your compliance team.

[05:23] Liam: We also requested an extended retention for error traces around the incident window; the default retention expired earlier than we'd like. Can you provide a snapshot?

[05:30] Priya: Yes — we'll export the traces and extend the short-term retention for your account for one month. We'll share access URL.

[05:38] Samira: Quick note on communication cadence: we'll share a customer-facing postmortem draft by 2026-12-19. Can we get feedback in 48 hours?

[05:45] Maya: 48 hours is fine.

[05:48] Diego: Now, I'd like to propose a joint benchmark run to validate under Nova-like load with representative prompts. We'll need three production prompt sets and a staging cluster that mirrors your config. Priya, can we get that scheduled?

[06:02] Priya: Yes — I'll slot the staging benchmark for the week of 2026-12-22; depends on Nova providing the prompt sets.

[06:09] Maya: We'll provide the sets by 2026-12-18. Also, please include KV cache metrics so we can see memory growth over time.

[06:17] Diego: We'll add memory, eviction, and per-tenant cache hit/miss and eviction latency metrics.

[06:24] Liam: A couple smaller items — our legal team asked about the incident impacting data residency. Any cross-region failovers happened?

[06:33] Samira: No cross-region failover for Nova. All requests were handled in your configured region. We will include region-by-region call counts in the postmortem appendix.

[06:43] Carlos: Any changes to billing because of the incident? We had a spike in retries and increased token usage.

[06:50] Priya: We'll compute the excess usage from retries and propose a credit; Samira will confirm with accounting and follow up.

[06:58] Maya: Also, what about runbook and on-call improvements? We want clearer escalation points.

[07:05] Diego: We're updating the runbook — adding explicit OOM sentinel triggers, automations to disable aggressive caching per-tenant, and clearer signals for the on-call to follow. We'll share the draft runbook updates.

[07:18] Liam: Can we have a brief walkthrough of the updated runbook on the next call?

[07:22] Priya: Absolutely — we'll schedule a 30-minute runbook review with your on-call team the week after the benchmark.

[07:31] Samira: Anything from Nova about contractual or SLA concerns?

[07:35] Maya: We'll review SLO impact. If the postmortem shows we dropped below agreed SLO for embeddings, we may request SLA credits. We'll coordinate with Priya.

[07:45] Samira: Understood — we'll be transparent in the metrics.

[07:50] Diego: One more technical note — we've added an early OOM sentinel that will gracefully restart the process before the eviction path becomes inconsistent. That should reduce the window where fallbacks misbehave. We'll document the sentinel thresholds and allow them to be tenant-configurable in the future.

[08:10] Carlos: That sounds good. How will we validate the sentinel behavior?

[08:15] Diego: Staging benchmarks with synthetic memory growth scenarios and long-running prompt sets. We'll share the harness Diego's team will produce.

[08:25] Maya: Ok, next steps recap?

[08:28] Samira: Recap: Diego will produce repro steps and test harness; SE to share patch diffs; Priya to schedule benchmark and runbook review; Nova to provide prompt sets; Samira to share customer-facing postmortem draft. We'll also ship KMS/audit traces and compute potential usage credits.

[08:47] Liam: Thanks all — we appreciate the responsiveness. We'll jump on the benchmark once Priya proposes the time.

[08:55] Samira: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email and update the ticket with action items.

[09:00] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription quality: some speaker labels may be imprecise; occasional mis-heard acronyms (KMS as K M S), small disfluencies. References to internal build numbers and specific diffs are in the private SE notes and will be shared directly with Nova via secure link rather than in this transcript.
